Marathon Petroleum gained 1.46% today as oil prices held steady and U.S. refineries operated at 97.4% capacity—near maximum utilization. The company benefits when refineries run hot like this, since they convert crude into higher-margin products like gasoline and diesel. Over the past week, the stock has climbed 3.77%, tracking alongside steady crude prices around $84 a barrel domestically.

The broader backdrop is tightening oil supply. A U.S. Navy blockade has cut Iranian oil exports significantly as the administration pursues economic pressure rather than military action, which reduces competing crude flowing into global markets. With refineries already running near capacity and storage inventories moderate, tighter supply keeps prices elevated—a tailwind for refiners turning barrels into fuel.
